rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4, Figs 9-10 - the authors develop their own soil-water-balance/stochastic model of hydrant withdrawals and compare simulated daily volumes and hourly peak-period hydrographs with Venturimeter records (1990-1999) at the upstream end of district 10 of the Sinistra Ofanto scheme, Southern Italy.
rows.notes: The study reports no result on the investment cost of on-demand networks nor on whether on-demand systems guarantee supply during peak periods. What it shows is that a water-balance model with stochastic farmer behaviour reproduces measured daily withdrawn volumes well and reproduces hourly peak-period hydrograph patterns, though it sometimes generates hourly peaks higher than measured because network hydraulic constraints are not modelled. The only statement that on-demand systems best meet requirements is in the introduction and is cited from Labye et al. (1988) and Lamaddalena & Sagardoy (2000), not an own result. At most the study provides a tool to estimate peak-period design discharges, a precondition for sizing (and costing) a network that guarantees peak supply; hence marked upstream.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Model is calibrated against measured upstream discharges in one district; no economic or cost data are reported anywhere in the paper.
